description: The Department of Afro-American Studies offers a program of graduate study leading to the Master of Arts degree. This program is designed to provide students with an interdisciplinary foundation for the study of people of African descent in the United States and the Diaspora. The program provides students with the opportunity to develop their research and writing skills in a variety of fields, including literature, history, and the social sciences. The program is intended to prepare students for doctoral study in Afro-American studies or related fields in the humanities and social sciences. It also serves students who wish to pursue careers in education, law, journalism, public policy, or the arts.

Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of African Cultural Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Madison provides students with a site for the intensive study of African languages and expressive cultures. Our program is unique in its focus on the intersection of three major areas: linguistics, literature, and culture. We offer a Master of Arts and a Doctor of Philosophy. Students are expected to engage with all three areas, while specializing in one. The department is also known for its strong emphasis on language pedagogy and its commitment to the study of African languages as a key to understanding African cultures. The M.A. degree may be a finishing degree for students who wish to use their expertise in African cultural studies for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, or the private sector. It may also be a step toward the Ph.D. degree.
Program name: Master of Arts in African Cultural Studies
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of African Cultural Studies provides undergraduate and graduate students with a holistic understanding of African expressive cultures. Our faculty and students study the languages, literatures, and other cultural forms of Africa and the African diaspora. Our curriculum includes courses in over a dozen African languages and in the literatures and cultures of Africa and its diaspora. We take a wide-ranging approach to the study of the continent and its people, looking at both traditional and contemporary forms of expression. We are a community of scholars and students who are passionate about the study of Africa and its people. Our program is designed to provide students with a deep and nuanced understanding of African cultures, as well as the skills they need to pursue careers in a variety of fields, including academia, international development, journalism, and more. The Ph.D. program in African Cultural Studies is designed for students who wish to pursue advanced research in the field. Students work closely with faculty members to develop their own research projects, and they have the opportunity to participate in a variety of research seminars and workshops.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Our graduates are highly successful in securing positions in academia, government, and the private sector. The department offers a high-quality, research-oriented PhD program that provides students with the tools to conduct original research in agricultural, development, and environmental and natural resource economics.

description: Agroecology is the study of how ecological processes—such as nutrient cycling, predator/prey interactions, and competition—interact with social processes to impact the sustainability of our food systems. Our Master of Science program is a unique interdisciplinary program that draws on many departments and programs from across the campus. Students explore the diverse factors that influence the functioning of our food and fiber systems, including environmental, social, political and economic components.
Program Page url: https://agroecology.wisc.edu/people/students/

description: Agronomy is the study of plant-soil-climate interactions. The Department of Agronomy at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is home to internationally recognized faculty, many of whom have won major campus and professional honors. Faculty interests range from molecular biological studies of plant growth to ecological studies of agroecosystems. Research and teaching within the department emphasize two major areas: plant breeding and plant genetics; and crop physiology, production, and management. Within these areas, faculty specialize in such fields as sustainable agriculture, international agriculture, weed science, and biotechnology. Students are prepared for careers in agribusiness, crop consulting, university teaching and research, and state and federal agencies. Learning goals include: Articulates, critiques, or elaborates the theories, research methods, and approaches to inquiry or schools of practice in the field of study; Identifies sources and assembles evidence pertaining to questions or challenges in the field of study; Demonstrates understanding of the primary field of study in a historical, social, or global context; Selects and utilizes the most appropriate methodologies and practices; Evaluates or synthesizes information across disciplines to generate products and inform missions of agriculture; Communicates clearly in ways appropriate to the field of study; and Recognizes and applies principles of ethical and professional conduct.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Agronomy offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees in agronomy. Research areas include plant breeding and genetics, plant biotechnology, cropping systems, agroecology, bioenergy, and weed science. Many of these programs are interdisciplinary and involve faculty in other departments such as Horticulture, Plant Pathology, Soil Science, Entomology, Botany, and Biochemistry.

description: The Department of Animal and Dairy Sciences offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees in Animal and Dairy Sciences. Program strengths include nutrition, physiology, genetics, management, and animal welfare. Research focuses on a wide range of animal species including dairy cattle, beef cattle, swine, poultry, and laboratory animals. Students may choose to pursue a degree in Animal and Dairy Sciences or in one of the campus-wide interdisciplinary programs in which departmental faculty participate: the Endocrinology–Reproductive Physiology Program, the Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Nutritional Sciences, the Integrated Program in Biochemistry, the Cellular and Molecular Biology Program, and the Genetics Training Program.

description:
The Department of Astronomy offers a Ph.D. in astronomy and a M.S. in astronomy. The M.S. is primarily for students pursuing a Ph.D. in astronomy or a related field; students are not normally admitted for a terminal M.S. degree. Research is carried out in both observational and theoretical areas. Current observational research includes the interstellar medium, stellar atmospheres, white dwarf stars, binary stars, star formation, galactic structure, local group galaxies, and observational cosmology. Theoretical research includes star formation, solar physics, plasma astrophysics, and cosmology. Students also participate in the development of instrumentation for both ground-based and space-based telescopes.

The Astronomy Department is located on the top floors of Sterling Hall and the adjacent Chamberlin Hall. The department consists of 14 faculty, approximately 25 graduate students, 35 undergraduate students, and 25 research and support staff. The department also has strong ties to the Physics Department, with several members of that department also conducting research in astronomy and astrophysics.

The department is a major partner in the 10-meter Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). Research facilities also include the 3.5-meter WIYN telescope at Kitt Peak, Arizona, and the Washburn Observatory on the UW–Madison campus. Department members have a long history of participation in space astronomy including the Hubble Space Telescope, the Wisconsin Ultraviolet Photo-polarimeter Experiment (WUPPE) which flew twice on the space shuttle, and the development of the High Speed Photometer for Hubble.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Astronomy offers a Ph.D. degree in astronomy. Our graduate program is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of modern astrophysics and a deep understanding of a particular sub-field. The program emphasizes research, and students are encouraged to begin research early in their graduate career. The department offers a wide range of research opportunities in observational and theoretical astrophysics, as well as in instrumentation. Research areas include: star formation, interstellar and intergalactic medium, galaxy evolution, stellar populations, high-energy astrophysics, and instrumentation.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a professional program that prepares students for a career as an athletic trainer. Athletic trainers (ATs) are multi-skilled health care professionals who render service or treatment, under the direction of or in collaboration with a physician, in accordance with their education and training and the states' statutes, rules and regulations. As a part of the health care team, athletic training services include primary care, injury and illness prevention, wellness promotion and education, emergent care, examination and clinical diagnosis, therapeutic intervention, and rehabilitation of injuries and medical conditions. The program is a 24-month, year-round program that includes a rigorous combination of classroom, laboratory, and clinical education experiences.
Accreditation status: The University of Wisconsin–Madison’s Athletic Training Program is currently accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE). The program has been placed on Probation as of February 11, 2022, by the CAATE.

The program focuses on practical applications and professional development, rather than research. Students take a core curriculum in atmospheric and oceanic sciences, as well as elective courses in areas such as data science, communication, and business. Students also complete a professional project, which provides them with hands-on experience in their field of interest.

description: The Department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences (AOS) offers a high-quality program of graduate study and research leading to the M.S. and Ph.D. degrees. description: The Biological Systems Engineering (BSE) Department graduate program provides an opportunity for students to pursue advanced studies and research in several areas of engineering. These include: Machinery Systems Engineering; Food and Bioprocess Engineering; Natural Resources and Environmental Engineering; Energy and Sustainable Systems Engineering; and Health and Safety Engineering. This program offers a Master of Science and a Doctor of Philosophy degree. The BSE Department provides excellent laboratory, shop, and computing facilities for its research programs. Many research projects are also conducted in cooperation with other departments in the University and with the USDA Forest Products Laboratory. Financial support is available for most students in the form of research assistantships or fellowships. Applicants for graduate study should have completed a B.S. degree in an engineering discipline. Students with B.S. degrees in non-engineering fields may be admitted to the graduate program but must complete a set of engineering and science courses before they can be granted an engineering degree. A non-engineering graduate degree (M.S. in Biological Systems Engineering) is available for students not wishing to complete the required engineering and science coursework.

description: Biological systems engineering (BSE) is a profession that uses engineering and biological principles to design and develop processes and systems to improve the quality of life while protecting the environment and natural resources. The Ph.D. degree is primarily a research degree. The purpose is to prepare students for careers in research and development in industry, government, and academia. Faculty and students in BSE conduct research in four primary areas: Food and Bioprocess Engineering: applying engineering principles to biological systems to produce food and other products. Natural Resources and Environmental Engineering: protecting and restoring the environment through improved management of soil and water resources. Machinery Systems Engineering: designing and improving machines and systems for food production and processing. Structural Systems and Environmental Control: designing and managing the environment in buildings for plants, animals, and people. Graduate students in biological systems engineering come from many different backgrounds. Many have undergraduate degrees in an engineering discipline (biological, agricultural, civil, chemical, mechanical, etc.), but others come with backgrounds in such fields as biology, chemistry, physics, and food science.

Our scientist-practitioner-based program is designed to prepare counseling psychologists who are well-grounded in psychological research and theory and who can apply this knowledge in clinical, research, and teaching settings. We aim to train psychologists who can think critically about research and practice, who are committed to social justice, and who can work effectively with diverse populations.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA)

Students complete the degree in two years of residency. The program is intentionally small, admitting only twelve students each year—six in poetry and six in fiction. In addition to a very high level of artistic achievement, students are expected to show academic excellence. The MFA program's course of study is rigorous, including intensive writing workshops, creative writing pedagogy, and graduate-level courses in English and/or American literature. Students must also complete a creative thesis. To ensure that students receive a broad range of training in the field, students take courses from a variety of permanent and visiting faculty. description: The UW–Madison Master of Science in Curriculum and Instruction: Secondary Science Education is a 13-month program that leads to a Master of Science degree and Wisconsin certification to teach science in grades 4–12. Our program is for students who have an undergraduate degree in a science field (biology, chemistry, physics, etc.) and wish to become middle or high school science teachers. The program starts in mid-June and ends the following July. Our cohort-based program emphasizes teaching for social justice. It is designed around the idea that students best learn science by doing science. Our university-based courses are coordinated with field experiences (practicum and student teaching) in local middle and high schools. Students will be eligible for a Wisconsin science teaching license (grades 4–12) upon successful completion of the program. Because this program is for initial teacher certification, it is not intended for students who already hold a teaching license.

Students learn to navigate the complete product development lifecycle, from empathy and ideation to prototyping and market strategy. The program is a collaborative effort between five UW–Madison schools and colleges: College of Engineering, School of Business, School of Human Ecology, Information School, and School of Education (Art Department).

The MS program offers two named options: Graduate Foundations and Graduate Data Analysis. Both options require 30 credits of graduate-level coursework and can be completed in as little as one year. The Graduate Foundations option is designed for students who want to prepare for a PhD in economics or a related field, while the Graduate Data Analysis option is designed for students who want to develop the analytical and quantitative skills needed for careers in data analysis and policy research.

The PhD program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in academia, as well as for research positions in government and the private sector.

All students follow a program of study that includes a core of courses in their area, as well as a selection of courses in research methods and other areas of the department. Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/graduate.pdf

description:
Aerospace engineering is a specialized field of engineering that focuses on the design, development, and production of aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems. The M.S. in engineering mechanics with a named option in aerospace engineering provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles of aerospace engineering, including aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, and materials. Students in this program will learn to apply these principles to solve complex problems related to the design and performance of aerospace systems. 

The master of science (M.S.) in engineering mechanics (EM) provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of mechanics, including the study of forces and their effects on matter. Students in this program will learn to apply these principles to solve complex engineering problems, with a focus on areas such as solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, and dynamics. The program offers a range of courses in both theoretical and applied mechanics, as well as opportunities for research and professional development. Graduates of the program will be well-prepared for careers in a variety of industries, including aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing, as well as for further study in doctoral programs. description: The Engineering Mechanics (EM) program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison provides a holistic approach to graduate study. It allows students to focus on their research early in the program, while offering a wide range of courses in EM and related fields like physics, mathematics, and other engineering disciplines. The program provides a strong foundation in the fundamentals of mechanics, while also providing flexibility to tailor the program to a student’s interests. Students in the program have access to state-of-the-art research facilities and work with faculty members who are world-renowned in their fields. The program prepares students for careers in academia, industry, and government research laboratories.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

The Department of English provides an environment in which graduate students can further their knowledge of English and American literature and/or composition and rhetoric. Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Entomology offers a program of study leading to the Master of Science or Doctor of Philosophy degree. The department provides high-quality educational and research opportunities for graduate students, preparing them for careers in academia, industry, and government. It is one of the few departments in the country that has maintained its breadth across the discipline of entomology. Research in the department involves a wide range of topics at molecular and genetic, organismal, and ecosystem levels. Graduate students are trained in various aspects of insect biology including: physiology and biochemistry, molecular biology, ecology and evolution, taxonomy and systematics, apiculture, biological control, and integrated pest management.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Entomology offers graduate study leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. Major areas of research and teaching include: Vector biology; Ecology and biological control; Forest entomology; Global health; Genomics and molecular biology; Insect-microbe interactions; Integrated pest management (IPM); Pollinator biology; Taxonomy, evolution, and biodiversity; and Toxicology. Research within the department encompasses many levels of biological organization, from the molecular to the landscape. We offer a flexible curriculum that can be tailored to meet the needs of each student and prepare them for a wide variety of careers in academia, government, and the private sector.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Students gain the skills and credentials to manage complex environmental issues, including land use, biodiversity, and climate change. description: The Nelson Institute Master of Science in Environmental Studies is a highly flexible, interdisciplinary degree. Our students develop a personalized course of study, working with a faculty advisor to ensure it meets their personal and professional goals. This degree is ideal for students who want to address environmental issues from multiple perspectives, drawing on the natural and social sciences, as well as the humanities and arts.

Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Environment and Resources program (E&R) (formerly Land Resources) is designed for students who want to address environmental problems from an interdisciplinary perspective. The program provides a structure for students to develop an individualized, rigorous course of study that integrates several disciplines. Students work with a faculty committee of three (for M.S.) or five (for Ph.D.) members to design a course of study that meets the student's research interests and career goals. Students in the E&R program come from a wide range of backgrounds, including the natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, and professional fields.

description: The Nelson Institute Environment and Resources (E&R) graduate program is for students who want to develop a deep understanding of the complex, interdisciplinary nature of environmental problems. It is designed to allow students the flexibility to work with a faculty advisor to design a course of study that is rigorous, individualized, and interdisciplinary. The program attracts students from all over the world with diverse backgrounds and interests in environmental issues. Students go on to pursue careers in the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies was established in 1970 and was renamed in 2002 to honor former Wisconsin Governor and U.S. Senator Gaylord Nelson, the founder of Earth Day. The institute is a world leader in interdisciplinary environmental research, teaching, and public service. It serves as a campus-wide hub for environmental initiatives and has partnerships with more than 40 academic departments and programs across the UW–Madison campus.

Each student chooses their own research area and creates a unique course of study with their faculty advisor and committee. The program is flexible and allows students to draw on the expertise of faculty from across the UW–Madison campus. Graduates from the E&R program have gone on to careers in academia, government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Food Science offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees in food science. Students can pursue research-based or coursework-based M.S. degrees. Research is a major component of the research-based M.S. and Ph.D. programs. The purpose of these programs is to provide students with advanced training in the basic and applied sciences as they relate to food. Students are prepared for careers in the food industry, academia, and government. Active research programs exist in the following areas: food chemistry, including flavor chemistry, ingredient interactions, and water relations; food microbiology, including food safety, public health, and fermentation; food engineering, focusing on rheology and processing; and sensory analysis.

Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/food-science/food-science-ms/food-science-ms.pdf

Research in the department involves a wide range of topics, including food chemistry, food microbiology and safety, and food engineering/processing. Faculty members and students are engaged in research that addresses fundamental and applied problems in food science, with the ultimate goal of improving the quality, safety, and healthfulness of the food supply. The Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge necessary to conduct independent research and to lead research programs in academia, industry, or government. Students are required to complete a body of original research and to present their findings in a dissertation.

description: The Graduate Program in Genetics (informally known as the Genetics Training Program or GTP) is the PhD program of the Laboratory of Genetics. This structure creates a highly collaborative environment for genetics research and training. Research in the program spans many fields, including molecular genetics, genomics, developmental biology, cell biology, cancer genetics, neuroscience, evolution, and human and clinical genetics.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Geography at UW–Madison is one of the top-ranked geography departments in the nation. It is a large, diverse, and vibrant department. Our graduate program is organized into four major subfields: Physical Geography, Human Geography, People–Environment Geography, and Cartography and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). For more information on each of the subfields and the research being conducted by our faculty and students, please visit the department website. The Geography M.S. provides a foundation for the doctoral program and a range of career paths. Students take courses across the breadth of the department and work with a primary advisor and a faculty committee to develop and conduct an original research project (M.S. thesis).

The program is designed to develop the student's ability to conduct original research and to prepare them for careers in academia, government, or the private sector. The department's graduates have been highly successful in securing faculty positions at major research universities and liberal arts colleges, and in obtaining research and management positions in government agencies and private organizations.

description: Geological Engineering (GLE) is an interdisciplinary program within the College of Engineering. Students in the GLE program are typically from engineering or earth science backgrounds. The GLE program is designed to provide students with the necessary skills to address complex engineering problems involving the earth’s surface and subsurface.

description: The Department of Geosciences offers a master of science (MS) and doctor of philosophy (PhD) in geosciences. Our program offers world-class research opportunities across the geosciences including geochemistry, geophysics, hydrogeology, and surface processes, and sedimentary, structural, and igneous and metamorphic geology. Many programs are interdisciplinary, with links to the departments of atmospheric and oceanic sciences, botany, chemistry, civil and environmental engineering, geography, materials science and engineering, and physics, as well as the Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies. To support this research, the department maintains many sophisticated laboratories for research in geochemistry, geophysics, and hydrogeology.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Geoscience at the University of Wisconsin–Madison has a long-standing reputation for excellence. The department and its research facilities are located in the historic Weeks Hall for Geological Sciences, which includes classrooms, a research and instructional computer lab, the C.K. Leith Library of Geology and Geophysics, the Geology Museum, and many individual research labs. The department offers a wide range of graduate study leading to the master of science and the doctor of philosophy degrees in geoscience. Research areas include: biogeochemistry; crystal chemistry and mineral structure; economic geology; engineering geology; geochronology; geochemistry; geomorphology; geophysics; glaciology; hydrogeology; isotope geochemistry; limnology; mineralogy; paleoclimatology; paleontology and paleoecology; petrology; sedimentology and stratigraphy; structural geology; tectonics.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Our distinguished faculty is dedicated to providing students with a deep knowledge of the field, preparing them for careers as researchers and teachers. While the primary emphasis of the program is to prepare scholars and teachers for the university level, we also encourage students to seek out opportunities beyond the academy.

description: The University of Wisconsin–Madison is a world-class center for the study of history. Materials scientists and engineers create the materials that make new technologies possible. Faculty and students in MS&E work on a wide range of materials, including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and composites. MS&E is a critical field for many industries, including aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and medicine. MS&E graduates are in high demand by employers in both the public and private sectors. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering at UW-Madison is a leading center for MS&E research and education. The department has a world-class faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, and a strong track record of success. MS&E graduates from UW–Madison are well-prepared for careers in academia, industry, and government.

Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The PhD program in medical physics is a research-oriented degree designed to prepare students for careers in research, teaching, and clinical practice in the various subfields of medical physics. Students are required to complete a core curriculum of medical physics courses, as well as elective courses in their area of interest. Research is a major component of the PhD program, and students are expected to conduct original research under the guidance of a faculty member. The program provides students with the training needed for a career in medical physics, including the areas of radiation oncology physics, diagnostic imaging, imaging science, and health physics. Students receive a strong foundation in physics and its application to medicine, and gain research experience in their chosen area of specialization.
Accreditation status: The Medical Physics Graduate Program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Medical Physics Education Programs (CAMPEP).
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Microbiology Graduate Program is a research-based program leading to the master of science and doctor of philosophy degrees. The program is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to the field of microbiology, as well as in-depth training in a specific area of research. Students have the opportunity to work with faculty from a wide range of departments across the UW–Madison campus, including Bacteriology; Medical Microbiology and Immunology; Food Science; Civil and Environmental Engineering; Soil Science; Biomolecular Chemistry; Plant Pathology; and others. The program provides students with the tools and training they need to succeed in a variety of careers in academia, industry, and government.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Microbiology Doctoral Training Program (MDTP) is a joint graduate program between the Department of Bacteriology and the Department of Medical Microbiology & Immunology. The program provides excellence in graduate education in microbiology, preparing students for careers in academia, industry, and government. The PhD program offers a broad range of research opportunities across the spectrum of microbiology, including basic and applied research in areas such as microbial physiology, genetics, genomics, pathogenesis, immunology, virology, environmental microbiology, and biotechnology.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Molecular and Environmental Toxicology Center (METC) is a campus-wide program that provides a focus for toxicology research and graduate education at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The METC is administratively located in the School of Medicine and Public Health, and is affiliated with the Gaylord Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies. Over 50 faculty members from about 20 departments participate in the METC. Areas of study include cellular and molecular toxicology, carcinogenesis, ecotoxicology, clinical and diagnostic toxicology, and nutritional toxicology. The program leads to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees.
Program name: Master of Science in Molecular and Environmental Toxicology
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Molecular and environmental toxicology is the study of the effects of environmental contaminants on living organisms. It is a multidisciplinary field that includes such diverse areas as mammalian toxicology, environmental toxicology, and environmental health. The Molecular and Environmental Toxicology Center (METC) provides a focal point for this research and for graduate training at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The METC is an interdisciplinary program with more than 70 faculty members from more than 25 departments in various colleges and schools. This broad range of faculty research interests provides students with many research opportunities. The mission of the program is to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of toxicology and to prepare them for careers in research, teaching, and service. Students in the program are encouraged to develop an understanding of the mechanisms of toxicity at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels, and to apply this knowledge to address important environmental and human health problems.
Program name: PhD in Molecular and Environmental Toxicology
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Concentration name: Ethnomusicology, Historical Musicology, and Music Theory
description: The Mead Witter School of Music offers the master of arts in music with majors in ethnomusicology, historical musicology, and music theory. The Mead Witter School of Music is located in the beautiful George L. Mosse Humanities Building, which also houses the departments of Art and History. The Mead Witter School of Music provides many resources including a large number of practice rooms, a state-of-the-art recording studio, and several performance spaces ranging from the small and intimate to the 1,200-seat Mills Concert Hall. Music students at UW–Madison also benefit from a world-class library system. The Mills Music Library is one of the largest and most significant music libraries in the United States. Its collection includes more than 250,000 items, including books, scores, and recordings, and it is a member of the Big Ten Academic Alliance. Beyond the Mead Witter School of Music, students have access to the many resources of a large research university, including numerous lectures, concerts, and other cultural events. Madison is also a vibrant city with a rich cultural life, including a variety of musical organizations, museums, and theaters.
Accreditation status: The Mead Witter School of Music is a fully accredited member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/music/music-ma/

Concentration name: Composition, Conducting, Music Performance, Music Theory, Musicology, Piano Performance and Pedagogy
description: The Mead Witter School of Music offers the master of music degree in several areas: composition, conducting, musicology, music theory, music performance, and piano performance and pedagogy. These programs are designed for students who have completed a bachelor’s degree in music and who wish to pursue advanced training and specialization in a specific area of music. Each program has its own specific requirements, which include coursework, recitals, and/or a final project or thesis.
Accreditation status: The Mead Witter School of Music is a charter member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Mead Witter School of Music offers the doctor of philosophy (Ph.D.) in music with four options: composition, ethnomusicology, musicology, and music theory. The Ph.D. in music provides students with the highest level of professional training in music research and composition, with the goal of preparing them for careers in research, teaching, and other professional music-related fields.
Accreditation status: National Association of Schools of Music (NASM)
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/music/music-phd/music-phd.pdf

description: The Mead Witter School of Music offers the Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) degree in Performance (Piano, Voice, String, Brass, Woodwind, and Percussion instruments), Conducting (Choral, Orchestral, and Wind), and Composition. The DMA degree focuses on the development of the highest level of musicianship and creative talent. It is designed for students who are looking for professional careers as performers, conductors, or composers, and who also wish to be prepared for the demands of teaching at the college or university level. DMA students at the Mead Witter School of Music study with renowned faculty who are committed to artistic and academic excellence.
Accreditation status: The Mead Witter School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).
Program name: Doctor of Musical Arts in Music
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Neuroscience Training Program (NTP) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison was established in 1971. The program now has over 100 faculty members whose research interests range from molecular neurobiology to integrative systems physiology and even clinical neuroscience. The NTP is a multidisciplinary program leading to a Ph.D. in neuroscience. Our goal is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. Our students are drawn from a variety of backgrounds and are encouraged to design an individualized program of study that includes a set of core and elective courses. More than 100 faculty members from over 20 departments are available for research training. Research in the program is diverse, ranging from molecular and cellular neuroscience to systems, behavior, and clinical research. The NTP also holds a long-standing training grant from the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS).
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/medicine-public-health-school-wide/neuroscience-ms/

description: The Department of Engineering Physics offers a graduate program leading to the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in nuclear engineering and engineering physics. Faculty and students in the department engage in research in nuclear reactor physics and safety, fusion engineering and technology, plasma physics, radiation sciences and engineering, nuclear materials, nuclear security and nonproliferation, and heat transfer and fluid mechanics.
Program name: Master of Science in Nuclear Engineering and Engineering Physics
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Nuclear Engineering and Engineering Physics PhD program offers students the opportunity to perform research at the highest level in one of the nation’s top-ranked programs. Our students work alongside world-renowned faculty to solve some of the world’s most pressing problems, from developing new ways to diagnose and treat disease to creating the next generation of clean energy sources. Students in our program develop a deep understanding of the principles of nuclear engineering and engineering physics and the ability to conduct independent, original research.
Program name: PhD in Nuclear Engineering and Engineering Physics
Program Page url: https://engineering.wisc.edu/programs/degrees/nuclear-engineering-and-engineering-physics-phd/

description: The Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is designed to prepare nurses for leadership roles in nursing education. The MSN program is a 30-credit, online program that can be completed in two years of part-time study. Students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to teach in academic or clinical settings, design curricula, and evaluate learning outcomes.
Accreditation status: The master’s degree program in nursing at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org).
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The PhD program at the UW–Madison School of Nursing prepares nurses as scientists, educators, and leaders for the advancement of nursing science. Our graduates are leaders in academia, government, and clinical research. Our students are mentored by world-class faculty in a research-intensive environment that values innovation and collaboration. The program is research-focused for those interested in advancing nursing science, conducting research, and teaching.
Program Page url: https://students.nursing.wisc.edu/graduate-advising/grad/

Concentration name: Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric–Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, Pediatric Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, Population Health, Systems Leadership and Innovation
description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) is a clinical doctorate designed for nurses who want to lead and innovate in health care. The program prepares graduates for the highest level of nursing practice by providing them with the skills to translate research into clinical practice, lead complex health systems, and influence health policy.
Accreditation status: The Doctor of Nursing Practice program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org).
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The graduate program in nutritional sciences provides students with a broad knowledge of the field of nutritional sciences, while also allowing them to focus on a specific area of research. Students have access to a wide variety of faculty research programs ranging from the purely laboratory-based biochemical and molecular aspects of nutrition to the more applied human and clinical nutrition area, as well as community and international nutrition.
Program name: Master of Science in Nutritional Sciences
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Concentration name: Biochemical and Molecular Nutrition; Human Nutrition
description: The Graduate Program in Nutritional Sciences (GPNS) provides a program of study for the doctor of philosophy (Ph.D.) and master of science (M.S.) degrees. GPNS is an interdisciplinary program that includes faculty from across the UW–Madison campus including several schools and colleges. The program offers students the opportunity to choose between two tracks: Biochemical and Molecular Nutrition or Human Nutrition. The Biochemical and Molecular Nutrition track focuses on the biochemical, molecular, and physiological aspects of nutrition, while the Human Nutrition track focuses on the application of nutritional principles to human health and disease.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The UW–Madison Doctor of Occupational Therapy (OTD) program is a post-professional degree designed for the working therapist. The program is offered through a collaboration between the Occupational Therapy program at UW–Madison and the Occupational Therapy program at UW–Milwaukee. Our online program provides a flexible and convenient option for occupational therapists to pursue a clinical doctorate while still working. Our students gain advanced knowledge and skills in evidence-based practice, leadership, and specialty areas of practice. The program is designed to be completed in as few as two years of part-time study.
Program Page url: https://www.aota.org/education/find-a-school/postprofessional-programs-in-ot---doctorate-degree-level

description: The M.S. degree in Operations Research (MSOR) is a research-oriented degree that requires a thesis. It is intended for students who want to prepare for a career in research and development, or for further graduate study (PhD). A student in the MSOR program will work with a faculty advisor to define a research topic and complete a thesis. Many of the faculty in the Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering participate in this program. Research areas include: mathematical programming (linear, nonlinear, integer, stochastic, and large-scale optimization), stochastic processes, and simulation.
Program name: Master of Science in Operations Research
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/industrial-systems-engineering/industrial-engineering-ms/industrial-engineering-research-ms/

description: The Pharmaceutical Sciences M.S. is an 'en route' degree only, available to students already enrolled in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Ph.D. program. The Ph.D. program in pharmaceutical sciences provides a rigorous background in a range of scientific disciplines that are critical to the preparation of the next generation of pharmaceutical scientists. The program's interdisciplinary design is reflected in its four research cores: drug discovery, drug action, drug delivery, and drug outcomes and policy. Research in pharmaceutical sciences focuses on developing effective new drugs and therapies and identifying and managing the outcomes of their use. The program addresses the drug development process and includes researchers with interests in the discovery of new drug entities, the laboratory and clinical evaluation of drug activity, the design and development of drug delivery systems, and the study of the clinical, social, and economic impact of drug use.
Program name: Master of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Pharmaceutical Sciences PhD program is a campus-wide interdisciplinary program that provides students with a rigorous and well-rounded training in the field of pharmaceutical sciences. The program consists of three research cores: Drug Discovery, Drug Action, and Drug Delivery. Faculty members from various departments across the UW–Madison campus, including the School of Pharmacy, School of Medicine and Public Health, College of Engineering, and College of Agricultural and Life Sciences, participate in the program as trainers. Students in the program have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty and conduct cutting-edge research in areas such as drug design and synthesis, pharmacology and toxicology, pharmaceutics and drug delivery, and clinical pharmaceutical sciences. The program prepares students for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can contribute to the discovery and development of new drugs and therapies to improve human health.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/pharmacy-school-wide/pharmaceutical-sciences-phd/pharmaceutical-sciences-phd_admissionstext.pdf

Concentration name: Pharmaceutical Sciences; Social and Administrative Sciences in Pharmacy
description: The School of Pharmacy offers the doctor of philosophy (PhD) degree in pharmacy. Students must select one of two different tracks: pharmaceutical sciences or social and administrative sciences in pharmacy. Research in pharmaceutical sciences involves the development and testing of drug delivery systems, the discovery and characterization of drugs and their mechanisms of action, and the study of the disposition of drugs in the body. Research in social and administrative sciences in pharmacy involves the study of social, behavioral, and economic aspects of drug use and pharmaceutical care.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a four-year professional degree program that prepares students for a career as a pharmacist. The curriculum is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to provide high-quality pharmaceutical care to patients. Students learn about the science of drugs and their effects on the human body, as well as the practical aspects of pharmacy practice, such as medication therapy management, patient counseling, and healthcare systems. The program also emphasizes the importance of professional ethics, communication, and lifelong learning.
Accreditation status: The University of Wisconsin–Madison Doctor of Pharmacy program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE)
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/pharmacy/pharmacy-school-wide/

description: The Department of Philosophy offers a graduate program leading to the doctor of philosophy. Most students enter the program with the goal of earning the Ph.D. Although the department does not have a separate M.A. program, students may earn the M.A. degree while on the way to the Ph.D. Students are usually admitted for the fall semester only.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The graduate program in philosophy is designed to prepare students for careers as philosophers and teachers of philosophy. The program is specifically directed toward the Ph.D. degree. Although students may earn the M.A. degree along the way, the department does not have a separate M.A. program. Students who wish to pursue only an M.A. degree are not normally admitted. The Ph.D. program is designed to be completed in five to six years. During the first two years, students take courses to satisfy the department’s distribution requirements. After completing these requirements, students work with a faculty committee to prepare for and complete their preliminary examination. They then begin work on their doctoral dissertation.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/philosophy/

description: The Department of Physics has a long-standing reputation for being one of the top physics departments in the nation. It provides students with a wide range of research opportunities in both experimental and theoretical physics. Areas of research include astrophysics; atomic, molecular, and optical physics; biophysics; condensed matter physics; cosmology; high-energy physics; nuclear physics; plasma physics; and quantum information and computing. Graduate students have access to state-of-the-art facilities and are encouraged to collaborate with other departments and research centers.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/physics/physics-ms/physics-ms_text.pdf

description: The Department of Physics offers a program of graduate study leading to the doctor of philosophy degree. The Ph.D. is a research degree and the program is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of physics and to develop their capacity for independent research. The department provides research opportunities in several fields including astrophysics; atomic, molecular, and optical physics; biophysics; condensed matter physics; cosmology; high energy physics; neutrino physics; nuclear physics; particle physics; plasma physics; quantum information and computing; and string theory. Students may also take part in interdisciplinary research in areas such as applied physics, chemical physics, and material science.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/graduate/physics/physics_degreesmajorsdoctoralminorsgraduateprofessionalcertificatestext.pdf

description: The Department of Cell and Regenerative Biology offers a program of graduate study leading to the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in Physiology. The Graduate Program in Physiology provides students with a broad background in several areas of physiology and allows them to focus on a particular area of research through the selection of a faculty advisor and the completion of a research project/thesis. Faculty trainers in the program are drawn from many departments within the School of Medicine and Public Health, as well as other schools and colleges on the UW–Madison campus. Areas of research interest include cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, neurophysiology, and molecular/cellular physiology.
